name: Responsive breakpoint scrub
looks: A ruler along the top of a UI sample extends from a narrow width to a wide one, with small pill markers popping in at each breakpoint it crosses. As the ruler passes each marker, the sample reflows live: a stacked column springs apart into a row, each element settling into its new slot.
build: The ruler's width tweens on the clock; breakpoint ticks sit at percentages of its max width and fade/scale in as the ruler reaches them. The sample's elements interpolate x and width between narrow- and wide-layout slots, power2.inOut, in lockstep with the ruler. The active marker uses the accent colour; passed markers dim.
sound: A tick on each breakpoint crossed, pitched slightly higher each time.
prompt: Show a layout adapting to its container: a width ruler extends and crosses labelled breakpoints, and the sample beneath reflows live from a single stacked column into a row, in lockstep with the ruler. Make the reflow a real, legible layout change.
source: a Lism CSS release video in prompt-motion.com's gallery (prompt-motion.com/ddryo-loos-300829), studied 2026-10-09
